newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine foreign minister heads for France.
newsitem.headline: Argentine foreign minister heads for France.

text.p: Argentine Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella leaves Friday on an official trip to France, a ministry spokesman said.
Di Tella will be meeting his French counterpart Herve de Charett to prepare for French President Jacques Chirac's visit to Argentina March 16-17.

He will also preside over the sixth meeting of the Paris-based Argentine-French Great Commission where he will call for the strengthening of bilateral cultural, commercial and economic ties, the spokesman said.

No details of the agenda were provided by the two delegations but they were expected to discuss the transport of French radioactive waste through international waters and study the possibility of Argentina joining the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).

French embassy sources said Paris was also likely to express an interest in taking part in the privatization of airports and installation of radars in Argentina and the construction of a bridge linking Buenos Aires to the Uruguayan city of Colonia.
Asked if the sides would discuss the notorious case of two French nuns who went missing during the 1976-1983 Argentine dictatorship, the embassy sources said, "no comment."
France tried and sentenced former Argentine army captain Alfredo Astiz in absentia to life in prison for the murder of the nuns.
